thesisQuality.note: Scaled regulated utility infrastructure and contracted generation/storage serve durable electricity demand with demonstrated long-duration capital deployment; merger execution tempers the exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Regulated capital growth, earnings growth and project backlog support strong momentum, offset by capital intensity and financing sensitivity.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Independent market data shows roughly $157.7B market cap, ~17x trailing P/E and ~18.5x forward P/E, a reasonable growth-adjusted valuation rather than rare asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Transaction approvals, regulated investment and contracted project conversion are identifiable catalysts, but merger timing and conditions remain uncertain.

governancePower.note: Long operating/capital deployment history supports strong governance, while the large combination and affordability commitments add execution and allocation uncertainty.

alignment2036.note: Dependable electricity, grid investment, storage and diverse generation are foundational across multiple electrification, AI/data-center and industrial-growth futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Regulated utility, generation, storage and development capabilities create multiple demand engines, though they share power-market and financing exposure.

bottleneckControl.note: Regulated grid infrastructure and dependable generation/storage are scarce system-critical assets with long permitting/construction lead times and limited near-term substitutes.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified regulated and contracted power assets can perform across several demand scenarios, while financing/regulatory outcomes remain common sensitivities.

substitutionResilience.note: Generation technologies can substitute, but grid delivery and dependable electricity service remain necessary; portfolio breadth improves adaptation.

supplyChainResilience.note: Large diversified development scale supports procurement flexibility, but equipment, interconnection, permitting and construction dependencies remain material.

pricingPower.note: Regulated allowed returns and contracted assets protect economics better than commodity pricing, but commissions, affordability commitments and financing costs constrain unilateral pricing.

risk.note: Regulatory approval/conditions, financing costs, integration complexity and capital intensity can reduce realized returns despite durable power demand.

confidence.note: Recent issuer Q2 and transaction evidence covers operating and strategic facts and independent current market data covers valuation; final merger conditions and realized synergies remain unknown.

thesis: NextEra owns scaled, difficult-to-replace power infrastructure aligned with accelerating electricity demand; capital cost, regulation and merger execution determine how much structural demand converts to value.
keyRisk: Financing and regulatory costs can outrun allowed or contracted returns, particularly during a large integration cycle.
nextCatalyst: Dominion transaction regulatory milestones and Q3 2026 earnings/capital deployment updates.
